title: Accessibility Analyzer
purpose: A practical learning aid that helps designers make better decisions about image purpose, alt text, and accessible alternatives. It does not certify accessibility.

red.label: Red — Likely significant issue
red.meaning: A likely significant accessibility issue needs attention.

orange.label: Orange — Review needed
orange.meaning: Something warrants review, but its impact or the available information is limited or uncertain.

green.label: Green — Checks passed
green.meaning: The applicable checks passed, with no significant issues detected in the information provided.

insufficient.label: Not enough information to assess
insufficient.meaning: There is not enough context to make a reasonable judgement.

informative.label: Informative
informative.description: The image communicates information relevant to the content.
informative.example: A photo showing a workplace hazard or a chart communicating a trend.

decorative.label: Decorative
decorative.description: The image adds visual interest but does not communicate essential information.
decorative.example: An abstract flourish used only to decorate a slide.

functional.label: Functional
functional.description: The image is part of a control or link and communicates an action or destination.
functional.example: A search icon that activates a search function.

complex.label: Complex
complex.description: The image communicates detailed information, such as a chart, map, diagram, flowchart or infographic.
complex.example: An evacuation plan showing routes and an assembly point.

decorative_html_alt.description: For an HTML image confirmed to be decorative, an empty alt attribute (alt="") is generally appropriate. A missing alt attribute is not the same as an empty one.

functional_context.description: Assess the action or destination in context, including visible labels and other accessible names. An icon inside a clearly labelled control may not need its own descriptive alt text.

complex_equivalent.description: Essential information can be provided through alt text, a longer description, surrounding content, an accessible table, or a combination. Avoid unnecessary duplication.

limitations: The analyzer evaluates information entered by the designer; it does not inspect image pixels or independently verify image contents.
Rule-based findings are guidance, not a guarantee of accessibility or WCAG conformance.
A green indicator means no significant issue was detected by the checks performed, not that the content is certified accessible.

decorative_alt_present.title: Consider an empty alt attribute
decorative_alt_present.why: You identified this as a decorative HTML image, but descriptive alt text may cause assistive technology to announce information that adds no value.
decorative_alt_present.next_step: If the image truly adds no essential information, consider alt="". If it does contribute meaning, reconsider whether it is decorative.

functional_name_missing.title: The control's purpose may not be clear
functional_name_missing.why: The text describes the icon's appearance or does not identify the action or destination, and you indicated there is no other accessible name.
functional_name_missing.next_step: Use text that communicates the action or destination, or ensure the control has another accessible name.

purpose_conflict.title: Reconsider the image purpose
purpose_conflict.why: Your explanation suggests the image conveys information, but it is classified as decorative.
purpose_conflict.next_step: Reconsider the purpose selection before continuing. The analyzer will not automatically reclassify the image.
